cli.smoke.test.smoke: --daemon --supervise --log-file: the invoking process returns 0 only after ready, the log file is 0600 and carries the ready line, umount ends the daemon and the supervisor; a refused daemon mount reports its reason to the invoker

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A CLOSE BURST COALESCES ITS DRAINS (decision 0003 §AF) — no-open, no write cache: `log` written past inline (its close drains), then a shell holds it open for append and 200 forked `/bin/echo` children write a line each through it — every child's exit closes its copy, a FLUSH with custody ⇒ ONE drains (the first), the rest defer to the reclaim cadence's next tick (drains ≤ 2 + the windows the burst spanned, drains + deferred ≥ 200; drained each, they re-uploaded a whole block per close: 57,000× amplification measured) → the deferred custody lands (owed 0, parked 0) → kill -9 → fsck --offline clean → remount → every line there

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A DEAD MANAGER HOLDING A STRIPED HOT DIRECTORY (rung 10 recovery item 6) — A (the manager) mkdirs `hot` and flips it over K = 64 stripes (the explicit command: A holds the map and every stripe); B JOINED storms creates into it (every one shipped to A, keyed to its stripe) → kill -9 A mid-storm ⇒ B PARKS at T_self (park expiries 0) → remount A (the D0 ladder's same-host successor, term 2; its mount replays its own region — the map, the stripes, the shipped inserts) → B's reclaim lands in the grace window, the storm resumes into the same stripes → `ls` = `find` and the stat digest equal from A and B, every counted name listed → umount B, A → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (C17 clean)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A JOINER'S CLEAN UNMOUNT AND REJOIN while the manager stays up — mount A (the manager) → B JOINED writes inline, staged and striped files (sha list) → `umount` B (clean: every lease released, the page Free, every staged file promoted; A reads every file sha-equal) → B mounts again at the same mount point: JOINED as appender 1 again (its projection's rows naming appender 1 are a previous incarnation's — loaded unleased), every file of every cycle sha-equal on B, B writes more; three cycles → umount B, every file sha-equal on A → umount A → `fsck --offline --scrub` 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A MEMBER'S CACHED COPY OF ANOTHER MEMBER'S BLOCKS NEVER OUTLIVES THE BLOCKS' RE-USE (0003 §W.2) — two 192 MiB data volumes of 1 MiB blocks, no write cache (every write beyond inline striped) → mount A (the manager) + B JOINED (the dest lease off: its window reads are whole-block fills that deposit) → A writes `f` (two blocks, fsync'd) → B reads it until its tiers hold its blocks → A fills the set to ENOSPC → A `rm f`: the delete recalls B's token and B purges the blocks' keys before it acks (scoped purges ≥ 1 on B) → A writes `g` (two blocks, fsync'd) into the blocks the rm freed → B reads `g`: sha-equal to A's, never `f`'s bytes

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A NO-OPEN CLOSE IS THE WRITE-BACK DRAIN (decision 0003 §AF) — format (no write cache: a partial block parks in RAM) → mount with SQUEEZEFS_FUSE_NO_OPEN=1 (the daemon latches the connection at ready: its own `.stats` open, the ONE OPEN answered ENOSYS) → `g` written and read → 1 MiB + 1000 B into a fresh `f` (a CREATE: no RELEASE will ever come) and appended to `g` (no OPEN at all) by plain redirections → kill -9 the moment the last close returned: nothing parked, nothing owed, no RELEASE, ≥ 2 FLUSH drains, ONE OPEN → fsck --offline clean → remount → both files whole

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A STREAMING OVERWRITE NEVER WEDGES THE DAEMON — format (no write cache), one 1 GiB file laid down, then ONE job's QD16 1 MiB sequential O_DIRECT overwrite of it (fio where present, else the smoke's kernel-aio writer) long enough to drain the fresh supply and run on block-grant top-ups: every write answered inside the row's bound, fuse_op_watchdog_overdue 0, lock_ticked_reregisters 0, the gauges clean, an orderly unmount (rung-10-fsync-route: a top-up winner parked on its journal ticket under a same-lane minter's spin)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A STRIPED DIRECTORY ON ONE DAEMON — mkdir hot → the explicit flip (`user.squeezefs.stripes` = 64 through setxattr; getxattr answers 64, a plain directory ENODATA) → 10,000 creates key their stripes (dir_stripe_routed_mutations ≥ 10,000; D's own tree holds the 66 markers alone) → `ls | wc -l` = 10,000 and `find` = 10,001 (the K-way merge, every name once) → a 1,000-move rename storm across stripes, every target present, every source gone → stat's nlink folds a subdirectory in → rm -rf: the striped rmdir is ONE intent → umount → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (C17 clean)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: CUSTODY NO CLOSE COVERS IS DRAINED ONCE IDLE (decision 0003 §AF) — no-open, no write cache, the owed idle horizon at 0 (the seam), the connection latched at ready (no RELEASE would drain `m` either): a writer creates `m` and writes 1 MiB + 1000 B (a parked partial block) and holds its fd OPEN — no close, so no FLUSH follows the write: the class a mapping written back after its fd closed (`fuse_vma_close` at munmap) and an async write landing after its close share ⇒ the ino is owed → the reclaim cadence drains it (parked 0, owed 0, ONE idle drain, no FLUSH drain) → kill -9 with the fd still open → fsck --offline clean → remount → the bytes are there

cli.smoke.test.smoke: DEFRAG --fold AND --meta ON A LIVE MOUNT — format (64 KiB meta nodes, 1 MiB blocks) → three fsync'd striped files held OPEN with 12 sector-aligned 512 B writes parked as W2 extents (parked_extent_bytes ≥ 12 pages) → `defrag --fold <mp>` folds every one in place (12 page DMAs for 6 KiB of user bytes ≤ the §J 8× bound, parked_extent_bytes 0, every byte exact after the close) → a forest of 8,000 files cut to 800 and rewritten 4× → `defrag --meta --throttle 1` runs under the duty cycle: `job cancel` mid-run → cancelled; a second at throttle 1: `job pause` → paused → `resume` → running → kill -9 mid-job → remount adopts it and it completes by plan regeneration → compactions + merges ≥ 1, nodes walked after ≤ before, `fsck --online` 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: FSCK AND SCRUB — format → fill (dirs, 200 packed small files, hard links, three fsync'd 20 MiB files, a clone) → umount → `fsck --offline --scrub` 0 findings over every block → mount, 8-way storm, kill -9 → `fsck --offline` 0 findings → remount, clean umount → a planted stray reference is exactly [C3]+[C8] on its block (exit 1), `--repair` plans, `--repair --apply` releases it, clean → a planted orphan inode is exactly [C9], destroyed on apply, clean → `merge-reports` of two residue shards ≡ the whole run

cli.smoke.test.smoke: INVALIDATION COHERENCE ACROSS DAEMONS (decision 0003 §AB.2, §AG.2) — every TTL class at 60 s on both (a stale entry would outlive the row); B evicts every token entry right after its serve (`SQUEEZEFS_TEST_TOKEN_EVICT_AFTER_SERVE`: B holds NO entry when A's change lands): mount A, B JOINS (A's TTL law flips to PEERED, logged) → A caches a NEGATIVE `d/x`, B creates it in A's directory (a served step at A) ⇒ A sees it at once → B caches a negative `d/y`, A creates it ⇒ once B's notifier drained, B sees it (the recalled name) → B caches `d/x`, A unlinks it ⇒ B misses it → B caches `d/y` and a negative `d/z`, A renames y → z ⇒ B sees both → B caches z's mode, A chmods it ⇒ B's stat is fresh → B counts the recalled names and its kernel-pinned drops, no epoch owed on either

cli.smoke.test.smoke: KERNEL AIO on the plain mount (no shim): io_submit of 8 × 4 KiB PWRITEs into a fresh file (the inline → striped promotion under concurrent writes), again over the existing file, under O_DIRECT; every io_getevents res the page, byte-exact read-back — on a mount WITHOUT the write cache (every write beyond inline striped) and WITH it

cli.smoke.test.smoke: KILL -9 BETWEEN A PROMOTION'S COMMIT AND ITS RING RELEASE (the kill matrix's two-ring [C4]) — a 4 MiB staged file promoted to its own block, the daemon killed after the layout committed: (a) remount without fsck → rm → clean unmount destroys the corpse's record (0 FAILED) → fsck clean; (b) fsck --offline judges the device alone (the ring is the supervisor's custody) → the remount adopts the record its live file's layout no longer names → the file byte-exact → the clean unmount destroys it UNNAMED → the next mount recovers 0 → rm → fsck clean

cli.smoke.test.smoke: MutualTls on this kernel — `key tls-init`/`tls-issue` ×3 through the binary (OpenSSL verifies the chain, a foreign CA's leaf fails it) → a mount under SQUEEZEFS_WIRE_CHANNEL=mutual_tls: WITH the tls ULP it comes up (channel 1) and unmounts clean, WITHOUT it it REFUSES on the console naming the missing ULP (the record layer is the kernel's — never a userspace fall-back) → a CA-less mutual_tls refuses naming the CA → a mismatched key refuses → the plaintext mount of the same set serves and unmounts

cli.smoke.test.smoke: ONLINE FSCK THROUGH THE ADMIN LANE — the fill (dirs, 200 packed files, hard links, three fsync'd 20 MiB files) → `fsck --online` whole = 0 findings → `--shards 0/3, 1/3, 2/3` online (each report names its shard, each judges its residue) → `merge-reports` of the three ≡ the whole run (0 findings, the inode census summed exactly) → an 8-way `cp` storm with three online runs INSIDE it: 0 findings each (the zero-FP law under churn) → the two-daemon set: B JOINED creates 2,000 files and a tree under A's root → `fsck --online` on A reads B's slots as foreign-live and B's ring as a window (foreign_slot_scoped > 0), 0 findings; on B's mount the lane refuses by verdict (not the coordinator)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: O_TRUNC UNDER NO-OPEN TRUNCATES (decision 0003 §AF: INIT drops FUSE_ATOMIC_O_TRUNC, so the open's truncate is a SETATTR(size 0) under the size setter's guard — with the flag kept, the kernel skips that SETATTR and no OPEN carries it) — every TTL class at 60 s: on A, `: > f` over a non-empty file empties it; B JOINS; A writes `d/a`, B empties it with `: >` (B's SETATTR ships to the holder) ⇒ both read size 0 and no byte; B writes `d/b`, A empties it ⇒ both read 0

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE BLOCK-MAP TREE — a 1.5 GiB file at 1 MiB blocks crosses the inline cap: kill -9 mid-crossing (the test seam) → remount → records staged, head not flipped, C11 reports the residue → the rewrite re-crosses (the ratchet resumes, residue reconciled) → sha round trip across a remount → 4 KiB overwrites → truncate to 100 MiB (the sweep frees every block past the cut) → rm (the corpse sweep) → df baseline → C8/C11 clean

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE CONTROL ARM'S CLOSE DRAIN (SQUEEZEFS_FUSE_NO_OPEN=0) — the same writes; the asynchronous RELEASE drains the parked blocks after close(2) returned (observed: parked 0, no OPEN answered ENOSYS, no FLUSH drain) → kill -9 → fsck --offline clean → remount → both files whole

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE FLEET READ SHARD — mount A (the coordinator) + B JOINED with the fleet on: B enrolls at A as a READ worker over its own manager link (job_remote_workers 1 on A) → 1 GiB of fsync'd files, 512 MiB written on each side → `scrub --online <A>` partitions 2 ways: shard 0 on A online, shard 1 LEASED to B, run by B's engine over B's own plane (B's scrub_blocks_scanned grows, job_fleet_worker_shards 1), PROPOSED as read_shard_result and merged on A (dispatched 1 = completed 1, relocal 0; every block scanned, 0 findings) → `scrub --online --throttle 5` again: B's residue stretched by the duty cycle, kill -9 B inside it → A's departure expires the lease (fencing +1), the residue is LOST and the local view re-run (relocal 1), the job completes whole, 0 findings; the engagement counters per side

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE FLEET'S MERGED BLOCK CENSUS — mount A + B JOINED with the fleet on and B under the `SQUEEZEFS_TEST_SHIP_EVERY_FREE` seam (the reference's shape, 0002 row 500): B promotes 8 staged files into ONE pack by the fsync lever, `rm`s one tenant → the NONTERMINAL free ships to A, whose untracked arm frees and punches the pack under B's 7 live tenants (A: punches +1) → `fsck --online <A>` REPORTS it: B's custody census rides its proposal, the coordinator's merged lost arm names the freed-while-referenced block and its tenant, confirmed by a second census round (C2 lost, exit 1) → B remounted (its caches gone): the 7 tenants read back WRONG off the device → the seam OFF: the same `rm` stays local (A: punches unchanged), B remounted reads its 7 tenants sha-equal, `fsck --online` 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE HANDOVER DRAINS PARKED STAMPS (rung 10 item 4) — A (the manager) parks a size-neutral write's mtime on a file of slot S (the drain cadence held a minute away); B's 48 setattr ships on ANOTHER file of S dominate A's judge (holder ops read net of served ships) → A OFFERS the slot to B, pushed on B's renewal grant → B ACCEPTS over the wire → A's flush-then-transfer runs step 0: the parked stamp journaled BEFORE the gate (`meta_kv_times_handover_drained` ≥ 1, `meta_kv_times_echo_foreign_dropped` 0 on both) → B, the new holder, serves exactly the mtime A had promised; fsck clean

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE JOBS MATRIX — format (1 MiB blocks) → fill (packed, striped, a 1.5 GiB block-map file) → umount, clone, remount → `volume add-data <mp>` ONLINE (the new volume live, the rebalance on the fabric, `backend_fill_spread` ≤ 10 pp) → `volume remove-data <mp> d0` → `job pause/resume/throttle` live → the drain retires d0 (every block moved once; df within the window) → `undrain` refused after retire → `defrag --pack <mp>` on a half-empty pack → `remove-data d1` at 25 % → kill -9 mid-drain → remount adopts and completes it → `fsck --online` 0 findings → a second daemon enrolls as a REMOTE WORKER over TCP and runs a job → `fsck --offline` clean

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE JOINER-SIDE GRANT LEDGER — the holder's ledger capped at 8 open grants (the seam), 1 MiB blocks; B writes 24 files of one floor grant each (24 grants, three times the cap): every consumed grant RETIRES at B's renewal declaration (`block_grant_consumed_retired` ≥ files − cap = 16, the table's structural bound), `block_grant_deferred` 0 at A, `block_grant_topup_deferred` 0 and `block_grant_exhausted` 0 at B, `open_grants` ≤ the cap per volume throughout, B's window ≤ GRANTS_MAX ranges; every file whole from A

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE KILL MATRIX — kill -9 at 50/100/150 MiB of a 200 MiB dd and mid 8-way cp storm → fsck --offline clean → remount → every fsync'd file byte-exact, every page of an in-flight file exact or a hole, C8 zero drift, C2 nothing leaked or lost, rm → df baseline → fsck clean → status

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE KILL ROWS (a) — kill -9 B mid-`tar -x` into A's directory ⇒ A evicts B at T_owner, records the death, recovers its region (dead_members_acted ≡ recorded × regions held, rollbacks 0, the page recovered → free), every file B acked is whole on A → remount B under the same node (the same-node successor) sees them → B's FIRST cross-owner mkdir succeeds → A's `rm -rf` of the recovered tree completes; recall timeouts 0, tripwires 0 on both

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE KILL ROWS (b) — kill -9 A (the manager) mid-storm on B ⇒ B PARKS-AND-RECLAIMS at T_self (acks held at the pre-admission gate, park expiries 0) → remount A (the D0 ladder: the same-host dead-pid proof, A wins volume 0 again at term 2, the grace window open, the allocation leases taken over from the dead incarnation) → B's reclaim lands in the grace window, its manager link re-points, the held writes drain and every storm file is whole on both

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE KILL ROWS (c) — `appender clear` refuses a live-mounted set; after A's clean umount parks B and B is killed unrecovered, `appender clear <uri> 1` performs the operator path (the page Recovering{0}, the writer bring-up, the EARLY record, the leave) and `appenders` shows `recovering`; `appender clear <uri> 0` refuses; the next mount's poll recovers the region and `appenders` shows `free`

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE KVDA PAGE SINK — A holds the leases with its pages on volume 0 and every carve's delta in ring 0; B pulls grants (200 MiB dd), its renewals declare its windows (the joiner-side grant ledger retires the consumed ones) → kill -9 A with B's window outstanding → remount A: the same-node takeover folds the kept window onto the pages, the arm LOADS them, B's reclaim declaration ADOPTS its window — relearned 0 → B keeps minting from it, both files whole from A → fsck clean (C6/C13)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE KVDA PAGE SINK's fallback — the same row with the dying holder's page writes SKIPPED (the seam): the successor's stale pages carry no carve and the kept window was checkpointed away, so B's declaration RE-LEARNS its window (`block_grant_relearned_from_windows` ≥ 1 — the delta the pages otherwise make 0); no double allocation, both files whole, fsck clean

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE N-DAEMON POSTURE, the manager half — format (the symmetric default; meta + 2 data) → mount A: the listener is up, .stats names the pid and the wire endpoint, the durable endpoint:{0} record agrees → a second PROCESS dials A over TCP with the secret read off the device: JoinAppender, M rotor slots, a first touch, SlotBusy on A's native slot, a membership join → `appenders` lists its region Live and `clients` lists the member → a joiner that DIES is evicted at T_owner and its death recorded in the ledger → the live joiner releases, leaves (region Free) → `umount` signals A and A's own close detaches

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE ONLINE VOLUME ROW ACROSS DAEMONS — mount A (the manager) + B JOINED → `volume add-data --no-rebalance <A> d2` → B learns the generation bump at its next renewal (NO remount): the record pulled over the wire, d2 attached and armed on B (data_volumes 3, writer volumes 3, its generation = A's) → B writes 4 MiB files until one's stripe unit hashes onto d2 (B's writer row on d2 consumed grants A's holder row carved) and A reads every file back byte-exact → B removes them (the frees ship to A) → `volume remove-data <A> d2` → B flips d2 Draining at the bump and returns its window (24 more files on B place nothing there) → the drain retires d2 → B flips it Retired → closure on both → umount B, A

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE ORDERED LAW'S KILL ROW (decision 0003 §AL.5 with §AJ.4) — format (no write cache: a partial block parks in RAM), the write-back timer posture, every promotion's own block POISONED with 0xAA before its image grain lands (SQUEEZEFS_TEST_OWN_BLOCK_POISON: the bytes a recycled block's previous owner leaves where a block device elides its discard) → per step a 100 B file grows by one grain at byte 8,192 (the gap [100, 8192) crosses the poisoned tail) and the daemon is killed -9: the moment the write returned / once the timer landed it / after conv=fsync / after an fsynced growth and a truncate-up into the tail → fsck --offline clean → remount → the file at its last durable size (unsynced: 100 B or whole; fsynced: whole) and every byte below it its own, never the poison

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE READ VIEW — a 16 MiB striped file (no write cache), its custody landed; 512 random 4 KiB O_DIRECT reads (QD 8) byte-exact: every probe and every post-DMA recheck resolves off the per-ino view (read_view_hits ≥ 2 per read, no view miss after the first read's fill, at most the atime echo's refill); a truncate stales the view (a read at the old length is EOF, read_view_stale moved), an overwrite's publish stales it again (the new bytes read back), the must-stay-0 set clean

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE REKEY ROW — format (1 MiB blocks, lz4 + aes-256-gcm, key A) → fill (40 packed 64 KiB files, three fsync'd 20 MiB incompressible striped files, an 8 MiB compressible one) → umount/remount (the packs) → `defrag --rekey --encrypt-key B --throttle 50 <mp>` opens the window and sweeps every block onto B through the ONE mover while a write lands under B → the window closes (rekey_window_open 0, windows_closed 1, len drift 0), every file byte-exact → `config show` names B and no next key → a mount with key A refuses by id, with B serves every file → a second rotation to C at 10 % killed -9 mid-sweep → remount under B resolves C from the key dir, adopts the job, converges and flips to C → fsck --offline --scrub clean under C

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE REPLAY PROOF (charter §5.2 the ack point, decision 0003 §BB) — a `--daemon --supervise` mount under the landing-hold seam acks creates whose journal writes are never issued; kill -9 the daemon: the supervisor replays the journal tail to the device, barriers, and only then releases the writer guard; fsck clean; after the remount every acked create is present; the same creates on a FOREGROUND mount (no supervisor) are gone after its kill — the power-cut window; fsck clean

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE SHARED HOT DIRECTORY ACROSS DAEMONS — A (the manager) mkdirs `hot`; B JOINED storms creates into it ⇒ A's judge: B dominates past N_floor, the OFFER rides B's renewal grant, B accepts, the slot MOVES (slot_offers_pushed ≥ 1, slot_handovers 1 at A; A's census flips nothing — one creator) → A and a THIRD daemon C storm into `hot`, now B's ⇒ two creators past N_floor: B FLIPS it over K = 64 stripes, 21 supplied by A and 21 by C over `SupplyStripeInos` (one batch each), 22 minted by B; every later create keys a stripe and ships into a striping domain feed no window (handovers stay 1) → `ls | wc -l`, `find` and the (name, ino) digest of every entry EQUAL from A, B and C → kill -9 B (the holder of `hot` and 22 stripes) mid-storm ⇒ A evicts B at T_owner and recovers its region (hot's slot and B's stripes the manager's), every open intent rolls forward (stuck 0), the storms continue → the view equal from A and C → kill -9 C (a SUPPLIER: 21 stripes are records in its slot) mid-storm, C storming too (it dies holding guard scopes parked at A) ⇒ A evicts it, sweeps its scopes and recovers its region, the supplied stripes stand, every name listed → umount A → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (C17 clean: no mapped stripe lost)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE STAGED READ'S IDENTITY WINDOW — a 256 KiB staged file; an O_DIRECT read of its page 39 held by SQUEEZEFS_TEST_STAGED_READ_HOLD between its layout resolve and its ring lookup (the device-true ruler, so the read reaches the lane) while `sync -f` under the promote lever promotes the file into a pack (the packed layout committed, the ring entry released) → released: the page reads back as written, staged_payload_lost_reads 0, the file promoted; the hold and the sync on different CPUs' queues (red: 4 KiB of zeros and `staged payload unreachable`; fstests generic/127 under the lever, a host-wide sync)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE TRANSFORMED APPEND on a cache-less mount (decision 0003 §AK) — lz4, then aes-256-gcm: a file past the inline bound grows by 40 fsync'd 72 B appends and reads back exact (the write side seeded a transformed block's image through a block-sized buffer the chunk-sized read window refused: EIO at the first write past 4 KiB); a transformed block cannot be patched in place, so each drain lands the block's framed image whole — trimmed to its live bytes: ≤ the stored bound of the file's bytes per drain (8,192 B on aes-256-gcm for a 7,880 B file), where the untrimmed image of an encrypted set was the whole block; a read past the image's plaintext within EOF serves zeros

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE TWO-DAEMON MATRIX over MutualTls on KERNEL TLS — `key tls-init` + `tls-issue` ×2 → mount A (SQUEEZEFS_WIRE_CHANNEL=mutual_tls, node-a) → mount B (node-b) JOINED over TLS (.stats: channel 1, handshakes, 0 refusals) → A reads B's file under a token, B's write recalls it → B's mkdir under A's root (a cross-owner intent) → a 200 MiB dd on B, the sha from A equal (the Plaintext row's result) → 0 MAC failures and 0 refusals on both → a THIRD daemon under a FOREIGN CA is refused (its mount fails naming the CA, A counts tls_refused_untrusted) → a PLAINTEXT daemon is refused by name at the handshake bound (A counts plaintext_refused) → umount B, A; on a kernel without the tls ULP the row is the ledger's other_step skip

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE TWO-DAEMON MATRIX — mount A (the manager) → mount B as a SECOND PROCESS joined over TCP (no flock, the region over the wire, the page as its ledger) → `appenders`/`clients` show both → B creates 2,000 files in its own directories (0 lease conflicts, rotor mints) → A reads B's files under tokens (grants; the second read is served from the cache; a write on B recalls and A's third read is fresh) → `tar -x` on B into a directory A owns (cross-owner intents, 0 stuck, closure) → `chmod` from A on B's file (the record ship; B's stat sees it) → a 200 MiB `dd` on B (every block a ranged grant pulled from A; `df` per the rule on both; the sha round trip from A; A's O_DIRECT re-read of one window is a READ CACHE grain hit and B's size-changing rewrite recalls it — A's next read is fresh, 0 stale serves under the verify seam; `rm` ships the frees to A) → A writes 8 MiB into B's file (the promotion and every block-map merge SHIP as layout publishes to B, the size claim as one setattr; the sha equal on both) → closure + invariant tripwires 0 on both → umount B (page Free, the member row gone) → umount A

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE VIRTUAL INODES WITHOUT AN OPEN (decision 0003 §AF) — under no-open `.stats` is read through the page cache with no generation pin and no FOPEN_DIRECT_IO: 200 reads while a create storm moves every counter are each ONE whole JSON document whose length is exactly the st_size the same fd's fstat reported; two sequential opens read two generations (different inos, different bytes, each exact); a truncating open and a write are EACCES

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE WRITE CACHE'S RECALL (charter §6.1 coherence, 2026-10-21) — mount A (the manager) and B (joined over TCP): B writes a 64 KiB file (staged in B's write cache, never fsync'd) and A reads it at once: A's grant ask RECALLS B's residents of the ino — B promotes them before the page is served — and A reads the bytes (sha equal), never zeros (`staged_payload_lost_reads` 0 on A; B's `recall_promotions` 1); the reverse direction likewise; a second read of the same file asks no promotion (the record left the ring); A's own staged files stay staged when nobody foreign reads them (red before: A read 64 KiB of zeros, `staged_payload_lost_reads` 1)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: THE WRITE-BACK TIMER UNDER A WRITER STORM — the memory bound (decision 0003 §AJ): no write cache, SQUEEZEFS_PARKED_BUFFERS=8 (the budget's parked-buffer component), 16 writers each create, write 1 MiB + 1000 B (two write(2)s) and close 12 files (a partial block each, every close local): at every sample the parked buffers stay ≤ 8 and their bytes ≤ 8 blocks — a writer past the cap parks at the gate or lands the coldest custody itself (gate waits + cold flushes ≥ 1), nothing grows without bound → the storm ends, the timer lands the rest (owed 0, parked 0) → kill -9 → fsck --offline clean → remount → all 192 files whole
